items.title: 6.2.1 Equation of Tangent to a Circle (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 174-175: 6.2.1 (a) tangent to x^2 + y^2 = r^2, (b) tangent to the general circle, derived by implicit differentiation

blocks.text: Pichle sabaq mein hum ne dekha ke tangent likhne ke liye ek point aur ek slope chahiye. Is sabaq mein hum circle ke kisi point \(P(x_{1}, y_{1})\) par tangent ki equation ek dafa derive karenge (khud bana kar dekhenge ke kahan se aati hai), taa ke baad mein har sawal mein seedha formula laga sakein. Do circles lenge: pehle sab se saada circle jis ka centre origin par hai, phir general circle.
(a) Circle centered at origin: x² + y² = r²

Maan lijiye \(P(x_{1}, y_{1})\) circle ka ek point hai:
\[x^{2} + y^{2} = r^{2} \quad \text{...(i)}\]
Slope chahiye, aur slope derivative deta hai. Is liye dono sides ko \(x\) ke lihaz se differentiate karte hain:
\[2x + 2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\]
\[\Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{x}{y}\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yahan kya hua? Isay implicit differentiation kehte hain. Circle par \(y\) bhi \(x\) par depend karta hai, is liye \(y^{2}\) ka derivative sirf \(2y\) nahin balke \(2y\frac{dy}{dx}\) hai (chain rule). Aur \(r^{2}\) ek constant (na badalne wala number) hai, us ka derivative zero.
Faida yeh hai ke humein pehle \(y = \pm\sqrt{r^{2} - x^{2}}\) nikalne ki zaroorat nahin. Equation ko jaisi hai waisi differentiate kar diya, aur ek hi jawab circle ke upar wale aur neeche wale dono hisson ke liye kaam karta hai.

Point \(P(x_{1}, y_{1})\) par tangent ka slope, \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) mein \(x = x_{1}\), \(y = y_{1}\) rakhne se:
\[m_{T} = \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)_{(x_{1},\, y_{1})} = -\dfrac{x_{1}}{y_{1}}\]
Ab point-slope form lagate hain. Is liye \(P(x_{1}, y_{1})\) par tangent ki equation:
\[y - y_{1} = -\dfrac{x_{1}}{y_{1}}(x - x_{1}), \quad y_{1} \ne 0\]
\[xx_{1} + yy_{1} = x_{1}^{2} + y_{1}^{2} \quad \text{...(ii)}\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Kitab yahan ek chhota qadam chhor deti hai, hum use khol kar dekhte hain. Dono sides ko \(y_{1}\) se zarb dein (fraction khatam karne ke liye):
\[y_{1}(y - y_{1}) = -x_{1}(x - x_{1})\]
\[yy_{1} - y_{1}^{2} = -xx_{1} + x_{1}^{2}\]
Ab \(xx_{1}\) ko left side par le aayein aur \(y_{1}^{2}\) ko right side par bhej dein (side badalne par sign badalta hai). Yahi (ii) hai.

Ab ek aur baat istemal karte hain: \(P(x_{1}, y_{1})\) circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} = r^{2}\) par para hai, to us ke coordinates circle ki equation ko poora karte hain:
\[x_{1}^{2} + y_{1}^{2} = r^{2} \quad \text{...(iii)}\]
(ii) ki right side mein (iii) rakhne se tangent ki matlooba (required) equation mil jati hai:

blocks.text_alt: x times x1 plus y times y1 equals r squared

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Shart \(y_{1} \ne 0\) kyun lagayi? Points \((\pm r, 0)\) par \(y_{1} = 0\) hai, to slope \(-\frac{x_{1}}{y_{1}}\) mein zero se taqseem ho jati hai, yani slope exist hi nahin karta. Wahan tangent vertical (khari) line hai. Lekin aakhri formula phir bhi theek kaam karta hai: \((r, 0)\) par yeh deta hai \(x \cdot r = r^{2}\), yani \(x = r\), jo bilkul wahi vertical tangent hai. Is liye \(xx_{1} + yy_{1} = r^{2}\) circle ke har point par sahi hai.
Geometry se tasdeeq: origin \(O\) se \(P\) tak radius ka slope \(\frac{y_{1}}{x_{1}}\) hai, aur \(\frac{y_{1}}{x_{1}} \times \left(-\frac{x_{1}}{y_{1}}\right) = -1\). Yani tangent radius par perpendicular hai, jaisa pichle sabaq mein kaha tha.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh misaal kitab ki nahin. Circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} = 25\) par point \((3, 4)\) par tangent nikaliye.
Pehle tasdeeq ke point circle par hai: \(9 + 16 = 25\). Theek.
Ab formula mein \(x_{1} = 3\), \(y_{1} = 4\), \(r^{2} = 25\) rakhiye:
\[3x + 4y = 25\]
Bas! Is ka slope \(-\frac{3}{4}\) hai aur radius \(OP\) ka slope \(\frac{4}{3}\); product \(-1\), yani perpendicular.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} = 16\) par point \((0, 4)\) par tangent kya hoga? (Jawab: \(0 \cdot x + 4y = 16\), yani \(y = 4\), ek horizontal line. Figure bana kar dekhiye, circle ke bilkul upar wala point hai.)

Ab wahi kaam general circle ke liye. Maan lijiye \(P(x_{1}, y_{1})\) is circle ka point hai:
\[x^{2} + y^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\]
Dono sides ko \(x\) ke lihaz se differentiate karte hain (\(2gx\) ka derivative \(2g\), \(2fy\) ka \(2f\frac{dy}{dx}\), aur \(c\) ka zero):
\[2x + 2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2g + 2f\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\]
\(\frac{dy}{dx}\) wale terms ek taraf, baqi doosri taraf:
\[2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2f\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -2x - 2g\]
Common nikaal kar:
\[2(y + f)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -2(x + g)\]
\[\Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{x + g}{y + f}\]
Point \(P(x_{1}, y_{1})\) par tangent ka slope:
\[m_{T} = \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)_{(x_{1},\, y_{1})} = -\dfrac{x_{1} + g}{y_{1} + f}\]
Is liye point-slope form se tangent ki equation:
\[y - y_{1} = -\dfrac{x_{1} + g}{y_{1} + f}(x - x_{1})\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Is slope ko geometry ki aankh se dekhiye: circle ka centre \(C(-g, -f)\) hai, to radius \(CP\) ka slope \(\frac{y_{1} - (-f)}{x_{1} - (-g)} = \frac{y_{1} + f}{x_{1} + g}\) hai. Tangent ka slope \(-\frac{x_{1} + g}{y_{1} + f}\) is ka ulta aur sign badla hua hai. Phir wahi baat: tangent radius par perpendicular.

Ab is equation ko saaf shakal dete hain. Dono sides ko \((y_{1} + f)\) se zarb dein:
\[(y - y_{1})(y_{1} + f) = -(x_{1} + g)(x - x_{1})\]
Dono brackets kholiye:
\[yy_{1} + fy - y_{1}^{2} - fy_{1}\]
\[= -xx_{1} + x_{1}^{2} - gx + gx_{1}\]
Terms ko tarteeb dein (rearranging): \(x\) aur \(y\) wale terms left par, baqi right par:
\[xx_{1} + yy_{1} + gx + fy\]
\[= x_{1}^{2} + y_{1}^{2} + gx_{1} + fy_{1}\]
Ab dono sides mein \(gx_{1} + fy_{1}\) jama (add) karein:
\[xx_{1} + yy_{1} + gx + gx_{1} + fy + fy_{1}\]
\[= x_{1}^{2} + y_{1}^{2} + 2gx_{1} + 2fy_{1} \quad \text{...(3)}\]
Kyun ke \(P(x_{1}, y_{1})\) circle par hai, is liye:
\[x_{1}^{2} + y_{1}^{2} + 2gx_{1} + 2fy_{1} + c = 0\]
\[\Rightarrow x_{1}^{2} + y_{1}^{2} + 2gx_{1} + 2fy_{1} = -c \quad \text{...(4)}\]
(4) ko (3) mein rakhein, \(-c\) ko left par le aayein aur terms ko jor kar likhein. Matlooba equation:

blocks.text_alt: x x1 plus y y1 plus g times (x plus x1) plus f times (y plus y1) plus c equals 0

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
\(gx_{1} + fy_{1}\) hi kyun jama kiya? Is liye ke is ke baad right side bilkul circle ki equation ka left hissa ban jati hai (\(c\) ke baghair), jis ki value humein maloom hai: \(-c\). Yeh chaal \(x_{1}^{2}\) aur \(y_{1}^{2}\) ko ghayab kar deti hai aur ek saaf formula chhor deti hai. Jaise ghar ka hisaab: agar maloom ho ke kul kharch kitna hai to har cheez alag alag ginne ki zaroorat nahin.
Part (a) ki tarah yeh formula us case ko bhi sambhal leta hai jab \(y_{1} + f = 0\) ho, yani tangent vertical ho aur slope wali form na chal sake.
Ek achhi tasdeeq: \(g = f = 0\) aur \(c = -r^{2}\) rakhein to formula \(xx_{1} + yy_{1} - r^{2} = 0\) ban jata hai, jo part (a) hai. Yani (a) asal mein (b) ka ek khaas case hai.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} = r^{2}\) par \((x_{1}, y_{1})\) par tangent: \(xx_{1} + yy_{1} = r^{2}\).
2. Circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\) par \((x_{1}, y_{1})\) par tangent: \(xx_{1} + yy_{1} + g(x + x_{1}) + f(y + y_{1}) + c = 0\).
3. Dono formulas implicit differentiation aur point-slope form se bane; "point circle par hai" wali baat ne inhein saada kiya.
4. Tangent hamesha point of contact par radius ke perpendicular hota hai.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Aise point par formula lagana jo circle par hai hi nahin. Pehle \((x_{1}, y_{1})\) circle ki equation mein rakh kar tasdeeq kijiye.
2. \(g(x + x_{1})\) ki jagah \(2g(x + x_{1})\) likh dena. 2 pehle hi \(x + x_{1}\) mein "kharch" ho chuka hai.
3. Jab \(x^{2}\) aur \(y^{2}\) ke coefficients 1 na hon (maslan \(2x^{2} + 2y^{2} + \ldots\)) to seedha formula laga dena. Pehle poori equation ko us coefficient se taqseem kijiye.
